ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB\parallel CD$, $DE$ bisects $\angle ADC$ and intersects $BC$ at point $E$, $AE\perp DE$, $AB=4$, $AE=3$, and $\sin\angle CDE=\frac{3}{5}$. Then, what is the length of $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend $AE,DC$ to intersect at point $F$,\\
since $DE$ bisects $\angle ADC$ and $DE\perp AE$,\\
therefore $\angle ADE=\angle FDE$, $AE=EF$,\\
let $\angle ADE=\angle FDE=\alpha$\\
since $DE\perp AE$, $\sin\angle CDE=\frac{3}{5}$, $AB=4$, $AE=3$\\
therefore $\frac{AE}{AD}=\sin\alpha =\frac{3}{5}$\\
therefore $AD=5$\\
therefore $DE=\sqrt{AD^{2}-AE^{2}}=4$\\
since $AB\parallel CD$\\
therefore $\angle F=\angle BAE=90^\circ-\alpha$\\
since $DE\perp AE$\\
therefore $\angle DAE=90^\circ-\alpha$,\\
therefore $\angle F=\angle DAE=\angle EAB$\\
therefore $DF=AD=5$\\
In $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle FCE$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle BAE=\angle F\\
\angle AEB=\angle FEC\\
AE=FE
\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore $\triangle ABE\cong \triangle FCE$,\\
therefore $CF=AB=4$,\\
therefore $DC=DF-CF=5-4=\boxed{1}$,

raw_record.original_question: In quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB\parallel CD$, $DE$ bisects $\angle ADC$ and intersects $BC$ at point $E$, $AE\perp DE$, $AB=4$, $AE=3$, and $\sin\angle CDE=\frac{3}{5}$. What is the length of $CD$?
raw_record.answer: Extend $AE$ and $DC$ to intersect at point $F$. Since $DE$ bisects $\angle ADC$ and $DE\perp AE$, we have $\angle ADE=\angle FDE$ and $AE=EF$. Let $\angle ADE=\angle FDE=\alpha$. Since $DE\perp AE$ and $\sin\angle CDE=\frac{3}{5}$, we get $\frac{AE}{AD}=\sin\alpha=\frac{3}{5}$. With $AE=3$, it follows that $AD=5$. Then $DE=\sqrt{AD^2-AE^2}=4$. Since $AB\parallel CD$, $\angle F=\angle BAE=90^\circ-\alpha$. Also, since $DE\perp AE$, $\angle DAE=90^\circ-\alpha$, so $\angle F=\angle DAE=\angle EAB$. Therefore $DF=AD=5$. In $\triangle ABE$ and $\triangle FCE$, $\angle BAE=\angle F$, $\angle AEB=\angle FEC$, and $AE=FE$, so $\triangle ABE\cong\triangle FCE$. Hence $CF=AB=4$, and thus $DC=DF-CF=5-4=\boxed{1}$.

Image description: The figure is quadrilateral ABCD, with A above and slightly to the left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D on the right and slightly above; B, E, and C are on the same approximately horizontal base, with E located between B and C; the line segment from A to E goes downward, DE connects from E diagonally up to the right to D, and is located between DA and DC; AB and CD have the same direction, satisfying the condition AB ∥ CD.

Reasoning: Construct the auxiliary line according to the method, extend AE past E, and intersect the extension of DC at F. Because DE bisects ∠ADC, ∠ADE = ∠CDE. Also because F is on the extension of DC, ∠FDE = ∠CDE, therefore ∠ADE = ∠FDE. And AE ⟂ DE, F is on the extension of AE, so FE ⟂ DE. Thus △ADE and △FDE are symmetric about DE, or by right angles, common side DE, and equal included angles, they can be obtained congruent, therefore AE = EF, AD = DF.

Let ∠ADE = ∠CDE = α. It is known that sin∠CDE = 3/5, so sin α = 3/5. In right triangle ADE, sin α = AE/AD. Also AE = 3, so 3/AD = 3/5, obtaining AD = 5. Therefore DF = AD = 5.

Because AB ∥ CD, and F, C, D are collinear, AB ∥ CF. Also A, E, F are collinear, and B, E, C are collinear, therefore ∠BAE = ∠CFE, ∠AEB = ∠FEC. Together with AE = EF, △ABE ≅ △FCE can be obtained, so CF = AB = 4.

On the line D, C, F, C is located between D and F, therefore DF = DC + CF. Thus CD = DF − CF = 5 − 4 = 1.
